about: AI Workflow Hero was captured at 640x470 and kept as a specification rather than as a gallery image. The palette is deep green #1F2A1D underneath, set in Inter. The entry names the stack that produced the page (React and Tailwind CSS) rather than hiding it. Motion is 400ms transitions and cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), kept quiet enough that the copy still leads. Keep it open while you write: the 16,580-character brief is the part that transfers to your own page.

layout.title: A bar with nothing spare
layout.body: Navigation is a single row with no second level under it. A mobile overlay takes over below the tablet breakpoint. The bar sits over the 640x470 composition without a background of its own, so the media runs edge to edge underneath it.

layout.title: Every measurement is written down
layout.body: The layout works on absolute values rather than ratios: 10px spacing steps, 400ms transitions and cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1) easing. The brief states values rather than proportions, so the composition keeps its relationships when the copy changes length.

layout.title: Tracking tightens as it grows
layout.body: With Inter doing the work, the sizes step down hard from the headline to the supporting copy and letter-spacing tightens as the size grows, so the hierarchy is carried by type rather than colour. A face swap is safe as long as the sizes and weights stay where the brief put them. Check the scale in greyscale.

layout.title: One row, no drawers
layout.body: Keep the link count to four or five; the row is sized for that. The reference was captured at 640x470.

motion.title: Short, matched timings
motion.body: One duration covers the interactions (400ms using cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1)), which is what keeps hover and press reading as one system. The values are short enough to read as feedback rather than as animation.

motion.title: Pointers only where they help
motion.body: The page answers only where it can be acted on: hover states on the buttons and links rather than on every card. Feedback is limited to the controls, so the composition stays still around them.

editorial.title: What moves in AI Workflow Hero
editorial.body: Motion is limited to 400ms transitions, hover and press states and a live canvas. Nothing in the hero section animates for longer than the brief allows. Nothing animates for its own sake in this hero section.

editorial.title: How AI Workflow Hero sequences the first read
editorial.body: Attention is directed rather than left to chance. The sequence runs navigation, the announcement badge, the stats row, the feature list and the background clip, and each stop is sized against 10px spacing steps and 400ms transitions so nothing arrives out of order. A SaaS reader gets the offer before the options.

editorial.title: What this hero section gets right
editorial.body: Restraint costs you room for proof above the fold. This brief accepts that cost and spends the first screen on the offer, with 10px spacing steps and 400ms transitions fixed so a proof section can be added below without a rework. AI Workflow Hero states the offer once and lets the composition repeat it rather than adding a second claim.

faq.answer: The captured brief runs 16,580 characters and covers the frame, the type scale, the palette and the transitions. Copying it gives you that text, and sending it to Studio stages the same request with the page already described.

faq.question: How much of AI Workflow Hero depends on React and Tailwind CSS?
faq.answer: AI Workflow Hero was built in React and Tailwind CSS, and the entry says so for provenance. The brief describes positions, sizes and timings, so it rebuilds in any framework that can set type and place elements.

faq.question: What drives the motion in AI Workflow Hero?
faq.answer: Entrances and state changes are in the 400ms range using cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1). They are driven by state changes rather than a scroll library, and they never hold up the copy.
